technical-summary: Corrected an over-correction (RV443) and clarified the operation vocabulary. User challenge 'are LSPs not recipes as well?' was right: verified in services/recipes.py that the module docstring names 'language servers', that MCP_CONFIG/MODEL_CONFIG are already config-mutation recipe kinds, and that MODEL_CONFIG's docstring defines the pattern (recipe = lifecycle/status/dry_run wrapper; reconciliation in MO06 shared core). So LSP IS a config-mutation recipe like MCP/model; my earlier RV412 ratification ('purpose-built functions NOT recipes') overshot and is withdrawn. Synthesis: everything is a recipe; the contract spans provisioning and config-mutation ops; providers_api exposes a purpose-built named function per family as the requester ENTRY over the recipe (not a replacement). MA08 now adds an LSP_CONFIG recipe + providers_api.sync_provider_language_servers following the MODEL_CONFIG pattern. Second clarification (user question): install/uninstall/verify are NOT synonyms of configure/prune/status — the contract is one superset; install≠configure (whole vs scoped diff), uninstall≠prune (total vs scoped-ownership, shared-file reason), verify≠status (active check vs passive read), probe is a distinct precondition check; config recipes must not use install(). Recorded canonically in the schema-doc banner; MA16/MO02/MA00 notes and the layering memory updated.
